whatItIs.text: The chicken's dark, fattier leg meat — harder to overcook than breast, with more flavour per bite.

historyNote.text: Chicken's rise from luxury to everyday meat is recent: in 1800s America chicken was the expensive meat of prosperous families, and only a Second World War beef and pork shortage pushed daily consumption into the mainstream.

howToChoose.text: Bone-in, skin-on thighs are cheapest and most forgiving; skinless boneless for speed. Look for pink, glossy meat, not grey or sticky.

storage.text: Raw chicken goes cold on the bottom shelf, sealed away from other food, and cooks within the rulebook's window.

foodSafetyRef.note: raw-poultry storage and handling live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Cooked thighs shred beautifully for tacos, ramen, and fried rice; a leftover thigh is a lunch — chop it cold over greens or warm it in a pan with whatever sauce is open.

substitutions.note: leaner; watch the cook time or it dries
different animal, similar fat-rich forgiveness in braises
